title: Missing data and duplicates
summary: NaN and friends: counting, dropping and filling missing values, forward-filling within groups, and removing duplicate rows.
hints: `df.isna()` is a frame of booleans, and summing booleans counts the Trues: `df.isna().sum()` gives the missing count per column. Turn it into a dict of plain ints with `{col: int(n) for col, n in df.isna().sum().items()}`. `rows_with_missing`: `int(df.isna().any(axis=1).sum())`.

`drop_incomplete`: `df.dropna(subset=required)` only looks at those columns. `fill_defaults`: compute `round(df["temp"].mean(), 1)` first (mean skips NaN), then `df.fillna({"temp": mean, "humidity": 0, "note": "none"})`: a dict fills each column with its own value.

`forward_fill_temps`: `df.assign(temp=df.groupby("sensor")["temp"].ffill())`. Grouping first stops sensor B from inheriting sensor A's last reading. `dedupe`: `df.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)` keeps the first copy of each identical row.
